full_description: TechGrove is the Centre of Excellence for Banyan Software, based in Chennai, India. TechGrove brings together India’s deep pool of technical talent with Banyan’s long-term approach to growth, creating a trusted, developer-focused environment where people can do their best work. About the role star/trac builds flow, a logistics platform for yards, gates and loading docks. It handles truck check-in, self- service terminals (kiosks), slot and dock planning, and real-time monitoring for industrial customers. We are moving flow from a single-tenant setup (WildFly, Oracle, one AWS account per customer, Elastic Beanstalk) to a cloud-native, multi-tenant platform: flow6, a multi-tenant flow API (Spring Boot, JDK 21) that serves many customers from one deployment, with strict tenant isolation flow-dynamic-ui, a configuration-driven frontend where pages, queries and forms are data, not code flow-terminal-service, the backend and configurator for our check-in kiosks An analytics and real-time layer: CDC from Postgres and Oracle into Apache Doris, Kafka (MSK), and live push to the UI much of our engineering runs through AI agents in Claude Code. Each agent has a written contract, hard rules and its own tools. Our infrastructure agents are DiVa, who works inside a workload account (EKS clusters, Dockerfiles, CI, GitOps deploys, image scans), and Otto, who works across the AWS Organization (accounts, SSO, shared networking, guardrails). They already do real work. They need a human principal who owns them. This role is that owner. You will run our platform end to end and set up what is still missing, with the agents doing much of the hands-on work under your direction. You will also keep making the agents better: safer, more capable, and more useful to the rest of the team. What you will do Own the platform Run our AWS estate: an AWS Organization with shared Networking, Monitoring and Shared Services accounts, plus customer workload accounts. EKS clusters (one per customer and environment, services as namespaces), ECR, RDS, MSK, Route 53. Own the deploy path end to end: GitLab CI from one standard template, then image build and scan, then a GitOps repo, then ArgoCD on EKS. Take new services to QA and then to production. Today that means flow6-mt, flow-dynamic-ui, the auth service and Keycloak. Make flow6 safe to run as several pods behind one service: per-tenant Quartz schedulers, database locking, cache invalidation across pods, and health and readiness probes. Set up what is missing Production secrets: External Secrets Operator with SSM Parameter Store and pod-level IAM roles (IRSA / Pod Identity), in place of hand-made Kubernetes Secrets. Identity: Keycloak for staff, the existing auth service for customers, and service accounts for system-to- system calls. Observability across accounts with Grafana, Prometheus and Loki. Alarms that are tuned, not noisy. The data platform: Apache Doris, CDC pipelines (Postgres logical replication, Oracle LogMiner), Kafka. Repeatable customer onboarding: account, SSO, VPC, monitoring. Cost governance and a clear view of what runs where and what it costs. Lead the infrastructure agents Own DiVa's and Otto's contracts: their scope, hard rules, process steps and handoffs to the other agents. Turn repeated manual work into skills: small, deterministic Python tools with read-only doctor / list / plan verbs and gated mutating verbs. Examples are Helm releases, kubectl apply, registry cleanup, and an AWS Organization skill. Keep and strengthen the safety rails: agents never delete, every change needs an up-front confirm that states cost and blast radius, guard hooks block destructive commands, and nothing goes to main without review. Check that agent output is correct. Read what they produce, test it against real systems, and fix the contract when an agent is wrong. Record decisions as Target Architecture Decisions (TADs) and keep the shared memory accurate and sourced. Be the principal Make infrastructure decisions on your own and write them down so others can follow. Work with the architects, backend and frontend developers, QA, and our Cloud Ops lead, who runs the existing customer environments. Mentor colleagues who are new to Kubernetes or to working with agents. What you bring Senior to principal-level experience in DevOps, SRE or platform engineering, including running production systems. AWS in depth: EKS, IAM (including cross-account roles and SSO / Identity Center), VPC design (including shared VPCs, RAM, peering and endpoints), ECR, RDS, Secrets Manager / SSM. Kubernetes in production: Helm or Kustomize, GitOps with ArgoCD, add-ons, network setup, rolling deploys. CI/CD: GitLab CI preferred, including self-hosted runners. Container builds with multi-stage Dockerfiles, BuildKit and image scanning (Amazon Inspector). The JVM in containers: Spring Boot services, Gradle / Maven builds, Artifactory. Databases from an operator's view: Postgres and Oracle; connection pools, migrations (Liquibase), password rotation. Scripting: Python and Bash, written to be clear, repeatable and safe. Hands-on work with AI coding agents (Claude Code or similar), or a strong wish to start. You treat an agent as a capable colleague whose work you check, not as a black box. Safety by default: least privilege, no secrets in repos or images, confirm before you mutate, and an understanding of what an SCP or a delete can break. Clear written English. German is a strong plus: many of our customers and colleagues work in German. Nice to have Multi-tenant SaaS platforms: tenant isolation, per-tenant data sources, "no tenant, no service" designs. Kafka / MSK, Apache Doris or another OLAP engine, Debezium or other CDC tooling. Keycloak and OAuth2 / OIDC. Grafana, Prometheus and Loki across several AWS accounts. Moving legacy Java EE (WildFly) workloads to containers. Proxmox / LXC or other on-prem CI infrastructure. Writing prompts, agent contracts, or evaluation suites for LLM agents. Your first 90 days 1. Weeks 1–4: Learn the estate and the agents. Run DiVa and Otto on real tasks. Write down where their contracts are thin or wrong, and fix the first gaps. 2. Weeks 5–8: Finish the QA rollout of the new stack (flow6-mt, flow-dynamic-ui, auth service, Keycloak hardening). Put production secrets handling (ESO + SSM + IRSA) in place. 3. Weeks 9–12: Agree a production readiness plan for multi-pod flow6 and the first production cluster with the team. Ship at least one new DiVa skill that removes a manual step from that path. The ideal candidate is a proven builder who has independently taken a substantial software service or application module from initial requirements through architecture, development, testing, deployment, and production support. You will contribute to an AI-assisted financial operations platform designed for fund controllers , supporting trial balances, reconciliation workflows, financial calculations, multi-level approvals, and accounting processes. This position requires strong backend engineering fundamentals, database architecture expertise, production AI agent development experience, and a commitment to financial data accuracy, consistency, and auditability. Key Responsibilities Backend Engineering & Architecture Design, develop, and maintain scalable, enterprise-grade backend applications. Own backend services throughout the complete software development lifecycle. Translate complex business requirements into technical specifications and architecture. Design robust REST APIs, application services, database schemas, and business logic. Implement authentication, authorization, role-based access control, and secure data access. Develop evaluation frameworks to measure AI agent accuracy, reliability, and performance. Integrate human-in-the-loop approval mechanisms for sensitive financial actions. Ensure AI agents retrieve information, identify exceptions, and support decision-making while deterministic backend services perform financial calculations. Persist agent workflow state, execution results, and relevant audit information in databases. Database, Infrastructure & Quality Engineering Design and implement scalable database architectures and optimized schemas. Work with PostgreSQL, Snowflake, and other enterprise data platforms. Implement infrastructure-as-code for consistent application deployments. Develop comprehensive unit and integration tests. Mock external services and network calls during automated testing. Maintain production quality through code reviews, performance optimization, and systematic debugging. Required Technical Skills Technology / Capability Requirements Backend Programming Python and Java; comparable enterprise backend technologies considered Python Frameworks FastAPI, Pydantic, SQLAlchemy Java Frameworks Spring Boot, Maven Databases PostgreSQL, Snowflake, database schema design API Development REST APIs, API contracts, versioning, idempotency, error handling Application Architecture Enterprise web services, domain modeling, service boundaries Security Authentication, authorization, role-based permissions Financial Data Handling Currency precision, decimal calculations, rounding, periods, time zones Development Methodology Specification-driven software development Cloud & Infrastructure Infrastructure as Code; Azure experience preferred Testing Unit testing, integration testing, mocking AI Engineering LLM agents, tool calling, workflow orchestration, structured outputs Agent Quality Evaluation frameworks, human approvals, persistent workflow state Mandatory Qualifications Minimum 5 years of professional backend software engineering experience. Proven experience independently architecting, building, and owning a complex production backend service or significant application module. Strong understanding of enterprise application architecture, API design, database modeling, and transactional integrity. Production backend development experience using Python, Java, or comparable technologies. Hands-on experience designing and implementing database architectures. Experience using written specifications to drive requirements, implementation, and verification. Demonstrated ability to deliver production-quality, thoroughly tested applications. Hands-on ownership of at least one production AI agent workflow, including LLM integration, tool calls, structured outputs, evaluations, and human-in-the-loop controls. Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and technical decision-making skills. Ability to work independently with business stakeholders and translate ambiguous requirements into working solutions. Important: Specific programming languages and frameworks are flexible for exceptional backend engineers who demonstrate genuine end-to-end ownership. Production AI agent development and substantial backend service ownership remain essential. Preferred Domain Experience Candidates with experience in one or more of the following areas will receive priority consideration: Private Equity, Private Credit, Hedge Funds, and Alternative Asset Management Fund Accounting, Fund Administration, and Portfolio Accounting Corporate Accounting, ERP, General Ledger, and Financial Close Management Banking, Capital Markets, BFSI, and Financial Technology Preferred Financial Knowledge General Ledger (GL), Journal Entries, and Trial Balance Net Asset Value (NAV), Valuations, and Financial Marks Accruals, Fee Calculations, and Period-End Close Financial Reconciliation and Exception Management Audit Trails, Financial Controls, and Maker-Checker Approval Workflows Additional Preferred Skills Microsoft Azure cloud platform. Production implementation of Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. Agentic AI solutions developed for accounting or financial workflows. Experience with high-volume, data-intensive financial applications. Experience designing systems with strict requirements for financial data correctness and auditability. Architectural judgment: Can explain design decisions, alternatives, and technical tradeoffs. Production accountability: Has handled real-world incidents, data issues, and performance challenges. Business understanding: Can collaborate directly with finance and accounting stakeholders. Engineering discipline: Prioritizes correctness, reliability, automated testing, and maintainability. Practical AI expertise: Has built real production AI workflows rather than only experimenting with LLM APIs. Ownership mindset: Can turn an ambiguous business problem into a deployed and supported technical solution. You figure things out with little hand-holding. You will work with leaders who will partner with you in the journey. Passion. Not the word on a resume — the evidence: a side project, a technology you went deep on, something you built because you wanted to. Depth. At least one thing you've built or debugged that you can explain down to the internals and the tradeoffs. For our people—Kyndryls—that means doing purposeful work that powers human progress. Join us and experience a flexible, supportive environment where your well-being is prioritized and your potential can thrive. The Role Infrastructure Architects are the key link between Kyndryl and our clients. You’re in a technical leadership role, uniting and guiding stakeholders from clients, governance, and project executives to delivery and sometimes even the vendors who work with the client. You’ll be there from the start of a project — understanding what’s needed and figuring out the best technical solution. And you’ll be there at the finish, delivering the right product on time and within budget. As an Infrastructure Architect, you’ll draw upon the full breadth of your talent and experience. This is a technical leadership role, so we want you to bring your vision, knowledge, and leadership to each project. To the client, you’re the subject matter expert – consulting early, gathering inputs, understanding what they need from our solution. You define what Kyndryl can do to meet this solution. You design the best solution for the job. And finally, you’re the tech leader for implementation. Responsibilities Architecture & Migration Leadership: Lead architecture workshops and design scalable GCP cloud solutions, including workload migration strategies from on-premises data centers to the cloud. Infrastructure as Code (IaC) & Automation: Build and deliver automated infrastructure, platform deployments, and configuration workflows using tools like Terraform, Ansible, Deployment Manager, and GitOps. CI/CD & DevSecOps Implementation: Design and set up secure, automated CI/CD pipelines leveraging both GCP native services (Cloud Build) and traditional DevOps tools (Jenkins, GitHub Actions, Argo, SonarQube). Optimization & Review: Perform periodic architecture reviews to enhance application performance, drive cost optimization, and build internal utilities for safer, high-speed engineering operations. Documentation & Governance: Document technical frameworks and architecture workflows while implementing robust monitoring, SRE practices, and configuration management (e.g., Anthos, GCVE). At Kyndryl we support all major cloud platforms, so you’ll get the chance to use everything you know – and then some. You’ll also become expert at knowing when and how to call on other SMEs outside your wheelhouse. Thinking your way around pre-existing limitations will grow your creativity and flexibility. You’ll learn a lot here, and if you want to work toward certifications there are plenty of opportunities.The rewards for all this are many. You’ll get to influence, create, and deliver something from start to finish. You will have the power to delight our clients. Your future at Kyndryl This role opens the door to many career paths, both vertical and horizontal, and there may be opportunity to travel. It’s a great chance for database administrators or other techs to break into the cloud. It’s also a solid path to become enterprise or chief architect or a distinguished engineer! Whatever you see for yourself, you’ll find the opportunity here. Who You Are You’re good at what you do and possess the required experience to prove it. However, equally as important – you have a growth mindset; keen to drive your own personal and professional development. You are customer-focused – someone who prioritizes customer success in their work. And finally, you’re open and borderless – naturally inclusive in how you work with others. Required Technical and Professional Experience Cloud Architecture (GCP/AWS): Hands-on experience designing multi-tier, fault-tolerant, cloud-native enterprise applications, primarily using GCP and secondarily AWS. Data Center & Infrastructure: Solid understanding of systems, storage, security, and networking across both traditional data center environments and public cloud (IaaS/PaaS). Infrastructure as Code & Automation: Experience automating infrastructure and configurations using tools like Terraform, Ansible, Chef, Puppet, and GitHub.
